title: Late-Time Observations of Type Ia Supernova SN 2014J with the Hubble Space Telescope Wide Field Camera 3
extended_summary:
This paper does not address education or generative AI. It presents late-time astronomical observations of Type Ia supernova SN 2014J using the Hubble Space Telescope Wide Field Camera 3. The study was motivated by questions about late-time supernova light-curve behavior, light-echo contamination, and whether late-time decline rates can be compared directly across supernovae to test proposed correlations with intrinsic luminosity.

The intervention or approach is complementary HST photometry in three filters (F438W, F555W, and F814W) taken between roughly 365 and 1296 days after peak B-band light. The author performs aperture photometry, checks for contamination from resolved and unresolved light echoes, and compares the resulting light curves to those of other well-studied Type Ia supernovae observed in similar bands. The analysis also includes linear fits to estimate decline rates over late-time intervals.

The paper concludes that SN 2014J’s late-time photometry is not contaminated by an unresolved light echo and that the new WFC3 measurements are consistent with previous ACS measurements in the overlapping green bandpass. It also finds that the observed late-time decline rates in F438W and F555W remain consistent with the previously reported trend that more luminous Type Ia supernovae decline more slowly at late times, though the author notes that the sample remains small and additional supernovae are needed for a definitive test.
